correctness.rationale: The two-contact trace identity reduces expected isotropic squared disagreement to n-3+p^T A p with A=I/2+C^TC/4 positive definite. The stationary point is normalized edge endpoint sums of w=(2I+CC^T)^{-1}1. For connected subcubic graphs, the fixed-point map F_v(w)=(1-sum_{u~v}w_u)/(d_v+2) sends [0,1/3]^V to itself and contracts by at most 3/5. Summing two endpoint equations gives w_u+w_v>=1/9; the normalizer is <=2m/3, yielding p_e>=1/(6m). The double-star orbit reduction and KKT conditions show its bridge probability is exactly zero for k>=3, uniquely by strict convexity; for k=3 the excess is 3b^2/4. A standard-library exact-rational checker replays 526 representative/exhaustive-small graphs; proof is universal and not based on finite enumeration.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The spectral-rate SDP uses the same projection matrices but a different function of probabilities and no fixed two-contact covariance objective. Periodic mixing-weight optimization changes the step operator and schedule, not this iid edge law. Neither is a stronger covering theorem. A general KKT method can derive an optimizer, but cannot establish the sharp all-graph degree cutoff without additional positivity analysis.

value.rationale: A network-design question distinct from optimizing long-term mixing: when a fixed iid short-budget pairwise averaging policy assigns zero probability to a possible contact, potentially removing connectivity. The all-graph subcubic full-support guarantee, explicit constructive resolvent and nonzero margin, together with a smallest-degree sharp disconnection mechanism, provide a natural structural boundary for feasible communication-network design. It is not merely an arithmetic restatement of the known quadratic loss formula.
